clue.text: Restricted time, perhaps, to break cover

indicators.note: one thing breaking another bursts into it, so the shuffled word sits inside the cover

parts.note: a lid is a cover for a pot or box

indicators.note: perhaps flags the word time as only one possible arrangement of its letters

explanation.surface: A short spell of time is said to be enough to blow someone's cover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Restricted time' reads as one phrase, but 'Restricted' alone is the definition; 'perhaps' rearranges TIME into MITE, which 'to break' sends into the cover.
explanation.definitionFit: Something restricted is kept within bounds, which is what limited means.

clue.text: Lordly demeanour of tour leader during row on ship

indicators.note: during means these letters fall inside the row

parts.note: a row is a line of things
taken as written

indicators.note: leader means the front letter of the word tour

parts.note: SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: A tour guide behaves grandly during a quarrel aboard a cruise ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' suggests a quarrel, but it is a line of things; 'leader' takes the first letter of tour, and 'during' places it with OF inside the row.
explanation.definitionFit: Loftiness is haughtiness, the superior bearing of a lord.

clue.text: North American is able to support state team

indicators.note: in a down clue the piece that supports sits underneath

parts.note: ME is the abbreviation for the US state of Maine
XI, eleven, is a cricket or football team
can means is able to

explanation.surface: An American can play for his state side.
explanation.definitionFit: Mexico is in North America, so a Mexican is a North American.

clue.text: Act with' elegance for audience, and entrance

indicators.note: for audience means the phrase is spoken to listeners and spelt by its sound

parts.note: a turn is an act on stage and style is elegance

explanation.surface: A performer plays gracefully for the crowd as they come in.
explanation.definitionFit: A turnstile is a revolving gate admitting one person at a time, an entrance to a ground.

clue.text: Curious set-up involving island queen

indicators.note: involving means the island is wrapped inside
in a down clue set up means read upwards, so the word is turned round

parts.note: odd means curious or strange

explanation.surface: A strange arrangement on an island involves its queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Dido was the legendary queen of Carthage in Virgil's Aeneid.

clue.text: Criticize a revolutionary display

parts.note: to pan a show is to criticise it harshly
Che Guevara is the archetypal revolutionary

explanation.surface: A critic attacks a showy rebel's flamboyant performance.
explanation.definitionFit: Panache is flamboyant style, a stylish display of confidence.

clue.text: Put aside for consideration in the recess?

explanation.surface: A proposal is shelved during the parliamentary holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recess' suggests a break from Parliament, but it is a small compartment.
explanation.definitionFit: To pigeonhole is to shelve something for later; a pigeonhole is also a small compartment in a desk or wall.

clue.text: Bond upset English, etc

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: etc means and so on

explanation.surface: A James Bond film upsets the English and others.
explanation.definitionFit: A noose is a loop that binds or ties, a bond in the sense of a fetter.

clue.text: The element is made from copper — claim

indicators.note: made from means these letters are the raw material, rearranged

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: Someone asserts an element is produced from copper.
explanation.definitionFit: Calcium is a chemical element, the metal found in bones and chalk.

clue.text: Mistake causes great alarm, though first away

indicators.note: first away means the opening letter is dropped

parts.note: terror is great fear or alarm

explanation.surface: A blunder causes panic, though the first reaction passes.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a blunder or slip in judgment or calculation.

clue.text: He makes arrangements to obtain a photographic preparation

explanation.surface: An arranger goes to collect chemicals for developing photographs.
explanation.definitionFit: A fixer is someone who arranges deals; in photography, fixer is the chemical bath that makes an image permanent.

clue.text: Boxer, possibly, in this servicemen's band?

definitions.text: Boxer, possibly, in this servicemen's band?

parts.words: Boxer, possibly, in this servicemen's band?
parts.note: a boxer dog wears a band round its neck, and men of the church who take services wear a white band at the throat

explanation.surface: Is a fighter perhaps playing in a military band?
explanation.walkthrough: 'servicemen' suggests soldiers, but here it means clergy who take church services.
explanation.definitionFit: The band worn by a dog round its neck and the stiff white clerical band of a priest share the same name.

clue.text: Make a cut in dimensions of a pub, say

indicators.note: say tells us the phrase is spoken, giving a word of the same sound

parts.note: a pub is an inn, and its dimensions are its size

explanation.surface: Someone measures a pub before knocking through a wall.
explanation.definitionFit: To incise is to cut into a surface, as with an engraving tool.

clue.text: Accommodating person going bust in the Loire

indicators.note: something going bust breaks apart, so these letters are scattered and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A guesthouse keeper goes bankrupt in the Loire valley.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotel keeper provides accommodation, so is literally an accommodating person.

clue.text: Resentment about troubles in dealing with rogues

indicators.note: about means one piece goes round the other

parts.note: pique is resentment at a slight
cares are worries or troubles

explanation.surface: Resentment grows over the trouble of handling villains.
explanation.definitionFit: A picaresque novel follows the adventures of a likeable scoundrel.

clue.text: Directions given by university, originally to inhibit apathy

parts.note: E and N are compass directions: east, north, north

indicators.note: originally points to the start of the next word, its opening letter

explanation.surface: Students given instructions by the university lose all motivation.
explanation.definitionFit: Ennui is listless boredom, a weary lack of interest close to apathy.

clue.text: In Bonn I hear the cardinal is sort of fly

parts.note: ich is German for I, and Bonn is in Germany

indicators.note: hear signals that the name is spoken and spelt by its sound

parts.note: Cardinal John Henry Newman, the Victorian churchman

explanation.surface: A German visitor reports hearing that a cardinal is an insect.
explanation.walkthrough: The ichneumon fly is a parasitic wasp.
explanation.definitionFit: The ichneumon fly is a parasitic wasp-like insect, a kind of fly in the older naming.

clue.text: Cameo isn't designed for a flatterer

indicators.note: designed means the letters are set out in a new pattern

explanation.surface: A cameo brooch is not made with a flatterer in mind.
explanation.definitionFit: An encomiast writes or speaks lavish praise, a eulogist.

clue.text: Diversion here for man on board, I hear — one in a suit

indicators.note: I hear marks the chess piece as spoken, spelt by its sound

parts.note: a knight is a chess piece, a man on the board
clubs is one of the four suits in cards

explanation.surface: A chess player wants entertainment, perhaps from a card game.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightclub is a place of late-night entertainment, a venue for diversion.

clue.text: Stumped, taking wicket during tie, then bat defensively

parts.note: ST is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for stumped

indicators.note: during means the wicket comes in the middle of the tied score

parts.note: a tie in a game, such as one-all
W is the cricket abbreviation for wicket

explanation.surface: A batsman, stumped while scores are level, should have played a dead bat.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, to stonewall is to bat purely to survive, without scoring.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket, a batsman who blocks every ball without attempting runs is said to stonewall.

clue.text: Well-behaved attendant

explanation.surface: A model hospital porter behaves impeccably.
explanation.definitionFit: Orderly means tidy and well-conducted; an orderly is a hospital attendant.

clue.text: Remain in contact, having caught fish together

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
ling is an edible sea fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: An angler stays in touch with friends after catching fish together.
explanation.definitionFit: To cling is to hold on tightly and stay attached.

clue.text: Personal claim of a friend in a Muslim territory?

parts.note: I'm, short for I am, is a claim about oneself
mate means friend

explanation.surface: Someone claims friendship in a Muslim land.
explanation.definitionFit: An imamate is the region ruled by an imam, a Muslim leader.

clue.text: The roots of political extremists, it's said

indicators.note: it's said marks the word as spoken, giving a word of the same sound

parts.note: radicals are those holding extreme political views

explanation.surface: Commentators blame the origins of the trouble on political extremists.
explanation.definitionFit: A radicle is the first root to emerge from a seed, so radicles are roots.

clue.text: Mad proposal to have gunners Midlands mounted on it

indicators.note: in a down clue mounted on means placed on top

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, the gunners
a bid is an offer or proposal

explanation.surface: A crazy plan puts artillery on top of a Midlands hill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Midlands' is a stray word from the newspaper scan and plays no part.
explanation.definitionFit: Rabid means fanatical or raving mad.

clue.text: Cold meat free from impurities

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps
lean is meat without fat

explanation.surface: Cold lean meat is pure.
explanation.definitionFit: Clean means spotless or uncontaminated.

clue.text: The little devil has skill to communicate

parts.note: an imp is a small mischievous devil
art means skill, as in the art of persuasion

explanation.surface: A mischievous child has a gift for getting the message across.
explanation.definitionFit: To impart is to pass on knowledge or news, to make it known.

clue.text: Military vehicle a magistrate ob- Scotland. served outside quarters

indicators.note: outside means the magistrate goes round the quarters

parts.note: JP, Justice of the Peace, is a magistrate
E, east, is one quarter of the compass; two give EE

explanation.surface: A magistrate is spotted in a military vehicle outside the barracks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ob- Scotland. served' is the word observed split by a stray word from the newspaper scan.
explanation.definitionFit: A jeep is a small rugged military vehicle.

clue.text: Bishop breaking rules? In France FLUMP that's material for satire

parts.note: B is the chess and abbreviation for bishop

indicators.note: breaking rules means the word rules is broken up and reshaped

parts.note: que means that in French, as the clue's In France tells us

explanation.surface: A bishop flouting the rules in France gives satirists plenty to work with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In France' marks the French word for 'that'; FLUMP is a stray word from the newspaper scan and plays no part. 'breaking' rearranges RULES into URLES.
explanation.definitionFit: Burlesque is mocking parody, so it supplies satire with its stuff.

clue.text: Help a girl left without one

indicators.note: without means outside, so the left letter stands beside the one

parts.note: Ava is a girl's name
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A girl left on her own needs help.
explanation.definitionFit: Avail as a noun means use or benefit, as in to no avail, so it stands for help.

clue.text: Preacher interrupted by the erstwhile senior member

indicators.note: interrupted by means the second piece breaks into the preacher's name

parts.note: John Donne, the poet, was Dean of St Paul's and a famous preacher
ye is an old form of the, as in Ye Olde Shoppe

explanation.surface: A preacher is interrupted by the former elder of the congregation.
explanation.definitionFit: A doyenne is the most respected or longest-serving woman in a group, its senior figure.

clue.text: Shoot a man — Basil, possibly

parts.note: to pot is to shoot game, as in taking a pot shot
Herb is a man's name, short for Herbert

explanation.surface: Someone is told to shoot a man called Basil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Basil' looks like a man's name, but it is the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Basil is an example of a leafy plant used in cooking.
